security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Mermaid syntax, Markdown code spans, and documentation labels. The package contains only Markdown reference files, and I found no executable shell, network, environment, filesystem, or prompt-injection behavior. The sensitive-looking /etc/passwd strings are quoted diagram labels used to explain escaping.

remediation.issue: Sensitive-looking sample paths appear inside diagram labels.
remediation.suggestion: Replace /etc/passwd examples with neutral placeholder paths to reduce scanner noise.

remediation.issue: Markdown backtick examples resemble shell execution to simple scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly fenced as Mermaid syntax and state that they are render-only documentation.

content.value_statement: Mermaid syntax can be difficult to remember when documenting complex systems in Obsidian. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for selecting and drafting Obsidian-ready diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable Mermaid diagram types for workflows, systems, data models, timelines, and charts.
Provides Obsidian-ready fenced Mermaid examples and syntax guidance.
Covers common diagrams plus beta formats such as architecture, block, Sankey, and XY charts.
Explains styling, classes, comments, themes, escaping, and multiline labels.
Documents Obsidian constraints, including disabled JavaScript callbacks and renderer differences.
Links quick-start examples to deeper per-diagram reference files.
limitations: It provides Mermaid guidance but does not execute or render diagrams outside Obsidian.
Some newer Mermaid features may not work in Obsidian bundled renderer.
Very large diagrams can render slowly and should be split into smaller views.
Export quality depends on Obsidian PDF and image rendering behavior.

use_cases.title: Document Engineering Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn process steps, service calls, and state transitions into readable diagrams for technical notes.

use_cases.title: Map Product Processes
use_cases.description: Create flowcharts, journeys, timelines, and quadrant charts that clarify decisions and roadmap tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Explain Data Relationships
use_cases.description: Describe entities, attributes, proportions, and flow magnitudes with ER, pie, Sankey, and XY diagrams.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first diagram from a simple process.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Mermaid flowchart for this process in Obsidian: [describe steps]. Use clear labels and one decision point.

prompt_templates.title: Sequence From Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert meeting notes into an interaction diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these meeting notes into a Mermaid sequence diagram for Obsidian: [notes]. Identify participants, messages, responses, and optional branches.

prompt_templates.title: Class Model Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Document a domain model for developers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Obsidian Mermaid class diagram for this domain model: [classes and relationships]. Include visibility markers, methods, inheritance, and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Diagram Choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Select and draft the best diagram for a complex system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best Mermaid diagram type for this architecture description, then create an Obsidian-ready diagram and explain the syntax choices: [system details].

output_examples.input: A signup flow with email verification and failure handling.
output_examples.output: A flowchart outline with start, validation, email verification, retry, success, and end states.

output_examples.input: Three services call an API and database during checkout.
output_examples.output: A sequence diagram plan naming each participant, request path, database query, response, and error branch.

output_examples.input: A product roadmap organized by quarter and release milestone.
output_examples.output: A timeline structure grouped by quarters with milestones, release notes, and major feature events.

best_practices: Start with the diagram type that matches the question, then add styling after the structure renders.
Keep node labels short, and use line breaks when Obsidian diagrams become hard to scan.
